content: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant commends the ‘remarkable resilience’, tech know-how, and awareness of social realities in the younger generation

title: We want people of Tamil Nadu to develop zero tolerance for corruption: CM Vijay
content: Delivering his I-Day address after hoisting the national flag at the ramparts of Fort St. George, CM Vijay thanked the people for breaking away from “caste and religious considerations” and rejecting “money and muscle power”

content: Dewaswom Minister  K. Muraleedharan directs Travancore Dewaswom Board to check the quality of ghee brought in by devotees

content: This indigenous device aims to reduce stent-related complications such as restenosis and thrombosis, featuring a patented design with 30-40% less metal than conventional stents.

content: Union says the former Minister’s actions have hurt the sentiments of the community and breached organisational discipline. Resolution argues that he owes his political ascent entirely to the NSS

title: Even as government considers MDR charge on UPI, data shows cash usage quickening in economy
content: An analysis by The Hindu shows that the growth in the value of UPI transactions has been consistently slowing since 2021-22, although the current rate of growth is still higher than that of cash with the public

title: Andhra Pradesh Deputy CM Pawan Kalyan opens  craft wood banks to supply raw material for six crafts

content: Constitutional values under strain, says Minister; calls for collective fight against discrimination, drug abuse and social inequality

title: Guard India’s unity, secular values: Basheer

title: CAG audit flags major gaps in Green India Mission implementation
content: The audit attributed the shortcomings to several factors, including inadequate convergence with other programmes, insufficient funding, deficiencies in planning and weak monitoring mechanisms

title: Caste abuses by politicians carry graver indignity: Karnataka High Court
content: Regrettably, the poison of caste sometimes finds expression even in the conduct of those who occupy positions of political power, though the Constitution has banished untouchability and promised equality, dignity and fraternity, the court observed.

title: Kerala start-up wins accolades for transforming tender coconut waste into opportunity
content: Pocket Grower, based in Karigannoor, Kollam, recycles discarded tender coconut waste into a soil-free potting mixture—a nutrient-rich growing medium for vegetables, fruits and ornamental plants; it recently won the Srishti ideathon held at College of Agriculture, Vellayani

title: Who is Tukaram Mundhe, the IAS officer leading Maharashtra’s FDA crackdown?
content: IAS officer Tukaram Mundhe, known for his frequent transfers and tough administrative style, is once again in the spotlight for his crackdown on food and drug adulteration as Maharashtra’s FDA Commissioner

title: Midnight wasn't the end: What happened in first few hours of Independent India
content: India's liberation from British rule was celebrated at midnight on August 15, 1947, as Jawaharlal Nehru captivated everyone with his famed 'Tryst with Destiny' speech. Following this historic moment, the newly formed government not only celebrated freedom but also faced daunting challenges related to governance and nation-building, with Lord Mountbatten taking charge as the first Governor-General during a time marked by the chaos of Partition.

title: What US, UK, Turkey and others think about India at 80
content: India's standing on the global stage reveals a mixed bag of perceptions among nations, with only 45% viewing it favorably. While Pakistan's outlook remains critical, Sri Lanka showcases significant support. Since 2025, favorability has waned in several countries, yet noteworthy improvements have emerged in Germany and the UK, highlighting the complexities and challenges of India's international reputation.

title: A ton of class! Devdutt Padikkal makes the long wait count
content: Devdutt Padikkal last played a Test for India during the 2024 Border-Gavaskar Trophy in Australia. After waiting 632 days, the left-hander seized his opportunity. Karnataka captaincy, role clarity and work on his game against spin reaped rewards as he put India in a dominant position with his maiden ton and a 150-run stand with his statemate and coffee partner KL Rahul on the opening day of the first Test in Galle.

title: OpenAI's S7 data centre drops plan to cool it with recycled water after permit snags
content: OpenAI has decided to discontinue its plans for implementing recycled water cooling at its Sydney data center due to regulatory hurdles that hindered the necessary pipeline's construction. Consequently, the facility will adopt a more energy-intensive closed-loop liquid cooling system. This transition comes amidst Sydney's growing demand for data centers. Notably, the S7 data center is projected to generate thousands of jobs during its construction phase.

title: Smartphone to be locked for missed EMI? RBI’s new rules explained
content: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has laid out some guidelines for lenders on recovery of loans, and whether they can block or lock the device that has been purchased via EMI financing. This new framework will come into effect from January 1, 2027.

title: US housing squeeze: Over 50% of families burdened by rent; here's how much tenants pay
content: Over 50% of renter families in America struggle with exorbitant housing costs, largely due to a chronic shortage of available homes that maintains high rental prices nationwide. Lower-income families bear the brunt of these escalating expenses, as zoning limitations and regulatory challenges obstruct new construction initiatives. Experts anticipate that upcoming housing legislation could eventually influence market pricing dynamics.

title: BWF World C'ships: Beyond smashes, drops, the conditions could decide the winner
content: At the BWF World Championships in Delhi, starting from Monday, the biggest challenge may not come from the opponent across the net. Drafts, heat and humidity could prove decisive as the world's best adapt to tricky conditions.

title: Zohran Mamdani’s ‘common sense regulation’ may push Amazon to move NYC deliveries
content: In a bold move, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has shown support for a groundbreaking bill that mandates direct employment for delivery drivers, aiming to eliminate subcontracting and bolster the rights of workers. However, Amazon has raised concerns, indicating the bill may drive its operations outside of the city.

title: Gurgaon’s annual road-repair cycle: 10 ways to fix the problem, not just the potholes
content: Gurgaon consistently suffers from road damage and waterlogging following significant monsoon rains. This ongoing issue highlights persistent drainage and construction flaws that have yet to be resolved. Despite ongoing investments in repairs, the city fails to tackle the fundamental causes of its infrastructure issues. Roads function within an interdependent network where adequate drainage is essential.

title: MacKenzie Scott helped abolish $40B in medical debt; how mechanics work
content: MacKenzie Scott is leading the charge in medical debt relief, having made groundbreaking donations that freed over $40 billion for families burdened by this often overwhelming responsibility. Her innovative approach, which involves acquiring debt at minimal costs for cancellation, has inspired other billionaires to make similar contributions. Yet, the call for broader policy reform lingers, revealing the constraints of this philanthropic model.

title: Shooting at US University leaves 5 injured, 1 critical; campus lockdown lifted
content: Virginia State University experienced a lockdown early Saturday following a shooting incident. Multiple suspects were involved, and several individuals sustained injuries near the Quad Annexes. Campus police confirmed that victims were transported to local hospitals for necessary medical treatment. Both university and county police are actively investigating the circumstances surrounding the shooting event. Authorities have not yet released specific details regarding the suspects or the injured parties.

title: 'Remove bulletproof glass or I wont speak': PM told officers ahead of 2014 I-Day
content: Former defence secretary RK Mathur has recalled how Prime Minister Narendra Modi insisted on removing the bulletproof glass barrier from the Red Fort before delivering his first Independence Day address as Prime Minister in 2014. Speaking about the episode, Mathur said he and the then Director of the Intelligence Bureau (IB) had briefed Modi about the security arrangements ahead of August 15.

title: Harmanpreet Singh's brace powers India to 3-1 win over Wales in World Cup opener
content: India began their FIH Hockey World Cup campaign with a strong 3-1 victory over Wales. Captain Harmanpreet Singh scored two goals, leading the team's dominant performance. Sanjay opened the scoring for India in the eighth minute of the match. Wales managed to pull one goal back late in the game. India secured three points from their opening Pool D fixture.

title: Patrick Mahomes, Brittany Mahomes' $5 million act builds lasting Texas legacy
content: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes' recent $5 million donation to Texas Tech marks a transformative moment for the university's football facilities. This substantial amount amplifies the fundraising efforts and ensures naming rights for prominent sections of the new complex. With Patrick's rich history at Texas Tech, their generosity underscores a lasting commitment to elevating the school's athletic programs to new heights.

title: Khabib Nurmagomedov sends special message to Islam Makhachev ahead of UFC 330
content: Khabib Nurmagomedov has praised Islam Makhachev's dedicated journey ahead of his significant welterweight title defense. Makhachev will face Ian Machado Garry at UFC 330 in Philadelphia this Saturday. While many expect Makhachev to win, Nurmagomedov respects Garry's fighting capabilities. Makhachev aims to extend his impressive winning streak to seventeen victories. Garry, an underdog, seeks to build his own significant fighting legacy.

title: Indian-American CEO who sacked 900 over Zoom gets fired himself
content: Indian-American entrepreneur Vishal Garg has been ousted as Better Home & Finance CEO.  The company cited concerns about his judgment and credibility after significant losses.  Garg's removal follows his controversial 2021 mass layoff of 900 employees.  He is now seeking to regain his position and is offering to work for one dollar annually.  Better's market value has significantly decreased since its pandemic-era peak.

title: Steve Smith creates history, equals Joe Root's world record in 124 Tests
content: In a thrilling display of skill, Steve Smith has matched Joe Root's remarkable world record for non-wicketkeeper Test catches, reaching 218 during the first Test against Bangladesh. Smith's achievement, accomplished with three catches at second slip, showcases his talent as he reaches this landmark in far fewer matches than Root. This puts Smith at the pinnacle of the all-time catching leaderboard.

title: USS Abraham Lincoln to return home amid rising scrutiny over sailor welfare
content: After an extended deployment, the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier is making its way home. While Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao minimized reports of sailor difficulties and supply deficiencies, the Navy contends that allegations regarding a mental health crisis aboard are overstated. This lengthy deployment highlights the pressures faced by the US Navy's carrier fleet, with the USS George Washington set to take over its operations in the Middle East.

title: Chandigarh police use tear gas to stop Qaumi Insaaf morcha march towards guv's house
content: Amid escalating tensions, law enforcement deployed tear gas and water cannons to scatter protesters intending to reach the Governor's residence. Clad in solidarity, attendees attempted to breach police barricades while advocating for the release of Sikh prisoners. The march, led by the Qaumi Insaaf Morcha, found support from multiple Sikh organizations, showcasing the strength of their campaign for the freedom of 'Bandi Singhs' at the Chandigarh-Mohali borders.

title: $70 million sale: How AI boom is pushing Silicon Valley luxury housing to new heights
content: A stunning estate in Silicon Valley has shattered records with its sale at an astonishing seventy million dollars, purchased by a visionary in the AI sector. This transaction not only marks the highest price for a home in Hillsborough but also underscores the profound impact of tech wealth on the area's luxury real estate market.

title: WATCH: Govinda reacts to Sunita Ahuja’s remarks
content: Govinda has made a public plea for his wife, Sunita Ahuja, to cease her use of foul language, notably phrases referencing mothers and sisters. Concerned about the effects of such behavior on impressionable youth, the actor highlighted the responsibilities of public figures. Sunita's frank comments about their life together have also caught the public's attention, igniting lively discussions among supporters.

title: 7.7 magnitude Indonesia quake: 38 killed, buildings collapse; 5 visuals of devastation
content: A significant earthquake registering 7.7 on the Richter scale rocked eastern Indonesia early Saturday, claiming the lives of at least thirty-eight individuals and leading to the destruction of various structures. Ongoing rescue missions are striving to aid the affected population, while landslides and widespread power failures hinder relief efforts in some areas. Although a tsunami alert was briefly raised, it was later cancelled after confirming that sea conditions were stable.

title: IPL cricketer Abishek Porel denied bail in alleged rape case
content: Abishek Porel, Delhi Capitals and Bengal cricketer, has been denied bail in an alleged rape and blackmail case involving a medical student. Arrested in Hooghly on August 11, he was sent to 14 days of judicial custody. The complainant alleged he promised marriage, later threatened to share private photos and illegally confined her during an April incident.

title: ‘Ireland’s Independence Day?’ Congress mocks PM Modi over Tricolour pocket square
content: In his post, Khera wrote, "Lagta hai sahib ne Urdu mein Tiranga pehna hai. Ya phir Bharat India ki jagah Ireland ka Independence Day mana rahay hain. (Looks like the sahib is wearing the Tricolour in Urdu. Or perhaps, instead of India, he is celebrating Ireland's Independence Day)." PM Modi delivered his 13th consecutive Independence Day address from the Red Fort, continuing a tradition that began  in 2014.

title: MP children fall ill in bid to set Tiranga yatra record
content: Twelve students fell ill after a Tiranga Yatra in Singrauli district. They reportedly waited nearly an hour for the state minister to arrive. Some students skipped breakfast and faced inadequate water arrangements during the event. Officials stated all students received treatment and were discharged later. Show-cause notices were issued to officials regarding the incident.

title: UK searches for homes with air conditioning jump 104% as heatwaves intensify
content: Searches for homes with air conditioning in the UK have more than doubled this summer. Repeated heatwaves prompt buyers to pay greater attention to property cooling capabilities. Many households are making practical changes to keep cool during hotter weather. Britain's housing stock faces concerns about coping with increasingly hotter summers. This shift influences buyer priorities and what they are willing to purchase.

title: 'Much remains to be done’: CJI urges young lawyers to shoulder responsibility of future
content: Chief Justice Surya Kant addressed young lawyers at the Supreme Court Bar Association's event. He acknowledged India's progress while stressing much remains to be done. The responsibility of the legal profession will soon rest on their shoulders. He highlighted the historical connection between law and India's freedom struggle. Young lawyers are encouraged to protect and carry forward justice institutions.

title: 'Awarapan 2' OTT release: When and where to stream Emraan Hashmi's film
content: The romantic thriller Awarapan 2, starring Emraan Hashmi and Disha Patani, released in theatres on August 14. A sequel to Hashmi's 2007 film 'Awarapan', the movie has already surpassed the lifetime collection of its predecessor on opening day itself, raking in over Rs. 21 crore at the box office despite stiff competition from 'Batwara 1947' and 'Vishwanath & Sons'. With its theatrical run now underway, here's where you'll be able to watch it online once it heads to streaming.

title: ‘Injury scare’ for Babar Azam ahead of England Tests as Pakistan captain rested
content: Pakistan captain Babar Azam sustained a hand injury during a warm-up match. He was forced to retire from the game as a precautionary measure. Azam is expected to return to training on Monday before the series begins. The three-Test series against England is scheduled to start on August 19. His availability remains a key talking point for the visiting team.

title: 'Pak's war crimes': Baloch activist posts video of 'missile debris', says 30 killed
content: Mir Yar Baloch has urged the US administration to impose sanctions on Pakistan and halt military support, including F-16 engine spare parts and upgrades to fighter jets and missile programmes. Pakistan's military has rejected the claim of an airstrike and said the casualties were caused by a premature explosion involving a vehicle-borne improvised explosive device allegedly being assembled by militants.

title: ‘School thik karo’: Dipke’s 1st audit flags gaps in Hingoli school - watch
content: Abhijeet Dipke launched the 'School Thik Karo' campaign in Santuk Pimpri village.  The campaign seeks a social audit of rural government schools nationwide.  It aims to identify and address issues like lack of water and poor sanitation.  Parents and residents will report deficiencies using a standardized assessment form.  The initiative focuses on essential facilities and improving the learning environment for students.

title: Bangladesh 6 wickets away from historic win as Australia stumble to 161/4
content: Bangladesh is on the brink of a remarkable Test win against Australia, needing just sixty-seven runs to secure victory with four wickets still in hand. Hasan Mahmud has played a pivotal role, claiming several key wickets for the team. Meanwhile, Mehidy Hasan Miraz has made significant contributions with both bat and ball, putting Australia in a tough position to salvage the match.

title: 'Public services neglected': CJP's new campaign to check facilities at public hospitals
content: The Cockroach Janata Party will launch a statewide campaign to assess the conditions in public hospitals.  This initiative follows their "School Thik Karo" campaign, which audits the amenities in government schools.  The party founder alleged that patients face long delays and poor facilities in public healthcare.  They aim to document infrastructure deficiencies and treatment access issues in hospitals.  Findings will be used to press for improvements in public education and healthcare.

title: Lucknow-Delhi Tejas becomes India's first privately branded train, 'Sprite' Tejas
content: The Lucknow-Delhi Tejas Express will be known as the Sprite Tejas Express from August 20. Coca-Cola's Sprite unit secured branding rights for the train's name and coaches. This move aims to generate non-fare revenue for the Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation. Other companies can also apply for branding on remaining coaches on a first-come basis. This initiative follows the railways' exploration of private participation in train operations.

content: The epicentre was located at Pematangsiantar, about 126 kilometres (78 miles) southeast of the island's capital Medan. It came hours after a 7.7 magnitude earthquake killed 47 in the country.

content: Global conflicts, tariffs and disruption around established trade routes have pushed shipping companies to look for alternatives. The Suez Canal route has become increasingly difficult to rely on.

content: The couple, identified as Sumant Jain, a civil engineer, and his wife Padmavathi, a software engineer, were involved in an argument that reportedly turned violent.

content: International organisations and the UN say the Taliban have struggled to address the natural and humanitarian crises Afghanistan has faced over the past five years, in part because Afghan women are under severe restrictions.

content: Indonesia experiences frequent earthquakes due to its location in the Pacific "Ring of Fire", an arc of intense seismic activity stretching from Japan through Southeast Asia and across the Pacific basin.

title: Meet Bianca Adler, 18, who turned back near Everest summit then made history
content: 18-year-old bianca Adler reached the 8,849-metre summit at 2:20am Nepal time . after an eight-hour climb from Camp 4 at 8,000 metres, she reached the summit alongside her guides, Pemba and Ngdu . the feat had eluded her just 12 months earlier .

title: Ukraine offers Black Sea shipping truce; Russia yet to respond : Report
content: a surge in strikes on ships and ports disrupts trade and raises concerns about global food supplies . the proposal was conveyed to Moscow through a third party . it comes as Russia and Ukraine accuse each other of escalating attacks on vessels and ports involved in exports .

title: Hawaii teen finds fungi in coconut husks that can biodegrade plastic
content: vera Wang was the first to look into using coconut waste to filter microplastics and sunscreen from seawater . two years later, her research has taken an interesting turn, with naturally occurring fungi in coconut husks that can break down plastic and sunscreen .

title: Strong tremor rocks Indonesia hours after 7.7 magnitude quake claims at least 38 lives
content: 7.7-magnitude quake struck off the coast of Indonesia's Flores region . the epicentre is located at 8.557°S latitude and 121.181°E longitude . at least 38 people were killed, buildings collapsed and communications disrupted .

title: 'I sincerely apologise': BCI chief to law students after row over NALSAR diktat
